section_summary: This section covers Japanese Antarctic whaling plans for the 1948–49 season and disputes over the limits and enforcement of Japanese fishing. It includes Chinese and Soviet complaints about fishing vessels, proposals for patrols, and competing U.S. views on extending Japanese fishing into the North Pacific and Pacific Trust Territory. Several memoranda compare Japanese fishery production estimates and debate conservation, security, and consultation with other countries.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1913 memorandum on the 1948–49 Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets operating, reporting, cargo, and inspection conditions for the expedition.
subfiles.summary: The concluding provisions require vessel markings, route notices, daily radio reports, cargo and fuel verification, and reports on whale oil. The authorization establishes no precedent for later whaling or territorial claims.

subfiles.title: Authorization of three Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets
subfiles.from: Hubert G. Schenck, Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: Recommends authorizing three Japanese fleets for the 1948–49 Antarctic season.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews the production and conduct of the first two postwar expeditions, Japan's food shortage, international catch limits, and likely objections from other whaling nations. It argues that Japanese operations have met acceptable efficiency and conservation standards, while noting vessel and fuel financing constraints. It recommends three factory ships and notification to the Department of the Army.

subfiles.title: Enforcement of directives limiting Japanese fishing areas
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards guidance on evidence needed to prosecute fishing-area violations.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a memorandum explaining the formal evidence Japanese courts require.

subfiles.title: Evidence for Japanese fishing-area violations
subfiles.about: Specifies documents needed for Japanese courts to convict fishing-area violators.
subfiles.summary: Requests signed observations and Chinese Government certification; states that SCAP enforces its high-seas directives.

subfiles.title: Proposed Japanese patrol of fishing areas
subfiles.about: Reports an emerging Japanese plan for government-operated fishing patrol vessels.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Japan may request authority for five or six patrol vessels to operate beyond the fishing limit.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese Antarctic whaling report to Norway
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Oslo
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding a SCAP report on the 1947–48 whaling season to the international statistics bureau.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the report for transmission to the International Bureau of Whaling Statistics in Sandefjord.

subfiles.title: Plan for the 1948–49 Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan's approved whaling plan and notes four additional vessels.
subfiles.summary: Reports approval of a two-fleet plan, soon to be issued as SCAPIN 1913A.

subfiles.title: Submission of Japanese Antarctic whaling plan
subfiles.from: Mamoru Hirakawa, Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry
subfiles.about: Submits Japan's 1948–49 Antarctic whaling plan for approval.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the plan required by SCAPIN 1913.

subfiles.title: The Antarctic whaling plan for the 1948–49 season
subfiles.about: Lists fleet vessels, managers, schedules, expected catches, materials, and cargo allocations.
subfiles.summary: The plan identifies two fleets totaling 29 vessels, their ports and sailing schedules, expected whale products, fuel and salt needs, and vessel cargoes. It also provides for chartering two catcher boats.

subfiles.title: Chinese representations concerning Japanese fishing operations
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese objections to violations and proposed Japanese fisheries patrols.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a conversation record and press items, then reports that five Japanese patrol vessels already operate within the authorized area. He says his mission will continue opposing approval of a Japanese patrol plan.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Chinese Mission on Japanese fishing violations
subfiles.about: Records Chinese concerns and SCAP discussion of patrols and prosecution.
subfiles.summary: Chinese representatives describe inadequate evidence for protests and oppose an unsupervised Japanese patrol outside authorized waters. Herrington explains court requirements and a proposed system of vessel reports and fisheries patrols.

subfiles.title: Japanese violate deep-sea fishing, SCAP expert says
subfiles.about: Reports Herrington's confirmation of repeated Japanese fishing-limit violations.
subfiles.summary: Reports SCAP's demand for stronger Japanese enforcement.

subfiles.title: A Matter of Good Faith
subfiles.about: Urges Japanese fishermen to obey existing fishing limits.
subfiles.summary: Argues that violations damage Japan's standing and that requests for expansion should follow proper channels.

subfiles.title: Request to declassify SANACC 99/4 conclusions
subfiles.about: Seeks lower classification so fishing-industry leaders can discuss proposed policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests declassification of selected conclusions from Secret to Restricted.

subfiles.title: Objections to declassifying SANACC 99/4
subfiles.about: Opposes sharing specific proposed policy with fishing-industry leaders.
subfiles.summary: Argues that selective industry consultation would be inequitable and that the proposed Restricted classification is inappropriate.

subfiles.title: Expediting papers on Japanese fishing and mandated territories
subfiles.about: Urges action on linked policy papers before Far Eastern Commission consideration.
subfiles.summary: Suggests asking Chapman to expedite SANACC 392/1 and SANACC 99/4.

subfiles.title: Further objection to declassifying SANACC 99/4 conclusions
subfiles.about: Argues that industry views can be sought without disclosing classified policy text.
subfiles.summary: Supports consultation on fishing questions but sees no need to release the paper's exact conclusions.

subfiles.title: British inquiry about observer on the 1948–49 whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Asks whether a British observer may join the expedition and who would pay expenses.
subfiles.summary: Requests continuation of the previous observer arrangement.

subfiles.title: Reply on British whaling observer
subfiles.about: Welcomes a British observer while assigning costs to the United Kingdom.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that Britain must meet the observer's salary and logistical expenses.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Australian Embassy on FEC issues
subfiles.about: Records Australian views on reparations shares, the yen rate, and Japanese fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: Bullock outlines a possible package for dividing shares and asks about the yen exchange rate. He says Australia strongly opposes extending Japanese fishing into the mandated islands.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government fishery monograph and SCAP comments
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese fishery study and Natural Resources Section's critique.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese study forecasts a substantial 1950 fish catch shortfall. SCAP's Natural Resources Section challenges its figures and estimates that improved use of fish for food could meet the earlier protein standard with a smaller catch.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section comments on Fishery Problems
subfiles.about: Critiques Japanese Government fishery statistics and projections.
subfiles.summary: The section disputes prewar and postwar catch figures, fleet size, material requirements, and the amount of fish needed to sustain food consumption. It considers a catch of about 3.6 million metric tons a practical 1950 goal if more fish is used as food. It warns that overstated projections could alarm other Pacific countries and reports that Japanese officials agreed to recheck the figures.

subfiles.title: State approval of SANACC 392/1 with amendment
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State member, SANACC
subfiles.about: Proposes qualified nondiscrimination in Trust Territory commercial fishing.
subfiles.summary: Approves the paper subject to security and inhabitants' welfare qualifications.

subfiles.title: Draft State approval of SANACC 392/1
subfiles.about: Drafts the State Department's qualified approval of Trust Territory fishing policy.
subfiles.summary: Drafts amended nondiscrimination language and proposes a press release.

subfiles.title: State amendments to SANACC 99/4
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State member, SANACC
subfiles.about: Proposes conservation rules and an eastward expansion of Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: The State Department proposes requiring Japanese operations to follow applicable whaling and marine conservation rules. It supports access to North Central Pacific albacore grounds while temporarily retaining the southern boundary of the authorized area.

subfiles.title: Draft amendments to SANACC 99/4
subfiles.about: Drafts limits on Japanese fishing expansion and gives reasons for excluding southern waters.
subfiles.summary: The draft proposes conservation language and an eastward extension into albacore grounds. It argues that immediate southern expansion would affect U.S. fisheries, naval interests, Trust Territory development, and relations with other FEC members.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on British whaling observer
subfiles.about: Accepts a British observer provided Britain pays salary and support costs.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the observer arrangement used on earlier expeditions.

subfiles.title: Routing of SCAP reply on British observer
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of SCAP's observer reply and discusses a missing earlier aide-mémoire.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the reply and notes the missing December 1947 State Department aide-mémoire.

subfiles.title: Copy of SCAP cable on British observer
subfiles.about: Repeats SCAP's acceptance of a British observer at British expense.
subfiles.summary: File copy of the September 24 cable.

subfiles.title: Additional copy of SCAP cable on British observer
subfiles.about: Repeats the conditions for a British observer on the whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Additional, poorly reproduced copy of the September 24 cable.

subfiles.title: SANACC 99/4 and Far Eastern Commission timing
subfiles.about: Records discussion of when SCAP could expand Japanese fishing eastward.
subfiles.summary: Keyes estimates a minimum three weeks for FEC action and discusses a six-week or sixty-day fallback.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing vessels outside the authorized area
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet seizures and protests near the Kurils, Hokkaido, and Sakhalin.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports twelve Soviet seizures of Japanese vessels, disputes some reported positions, and forwards a Soviet protest and his reply. He maintains that SCAP alone enforces its high-seas fishing limits and describes Japanese and U.S. patrol measures near eastern Hokkaido.

subfiles.title: Soviet protest over Japanese vessels
subfiles.from: K. N. Derevyanko, Soviet member, Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.about: Alleges Japanese violations of Soviet territorial waters and requests corrective measures.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko reports twelve detentions near Shikotan and Sakhalin, says nine vessels were released, and alleges deliberate entry by three others.

subfiles.title: Reply to Soviet protest over Japanese vessels
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, SCAP Diplomatic Section
subfiles.about: Asserts SCAP's authority over fishing-limit enforcement and requests certified evidence.
subfiles.summary: Sebald says the evidence does not establish every alleged territorial-water violation. He asks Soviet patrols to refrain from seizing Japanese vessels on the high seas and to submit certified reports for prosecution in Japan.

subfiles.title: Compromise on Japanese fishing in the Pacific Trust Territory
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Proposes conditions for eventual Japanese fishing in Trust Territory high seas.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman reviews Army proposals for rapid expansion and objections concerning conservation, security, administration, and consultation with FEC countries. He recommends allowing SCAP to authorize Trust Territory fishing once enforceable standards are in place, while shortening the proposed interval for northward expansion.

subfiles.title: Chapman memorandum opposing immediate southern expansion
subfiles.about: Supports eastward fishing expansion while opposing immediate access near the Trust Territory.
subfiles.summary: Chapman argues that southern expansion would provoke opposition among U.S. agencies, FEC members, Congress, and fishing interests. He recommends adopting the Navy–Interior position in SANACC 99/4.

subfiles.title: Nitze memorandum on Japanese fishing privileges in the Pacific Trust Territory
subfiles.about: Argues against excluding Japanese fishing without a clear security or administrative reason.
subfiles.summary: Nitze urges that any restriction rest on security or administrative grounds, with SCAP and the Navy assessing those grounds.
